provisional: set after the first green scale run (HARDEN-07, DEC-184)
_how: A budget is for 50,000 tracks (1,000 files for a tag write). A smaller run is held to it; a larger one is recorded, not held.
Base: the Windows number in docs/user-guide/performance.md times 1.5, or the Phase 15/16 budget where one exists.
A time under 10 ms is floored at 10 ms: below that a shared runner measures noise.
Where nothing was recorded (or the guide's number is out of date) the base is a first estimate from a Linux container run, said so in _basis.
A leg's scale multiplies every time budget (the Intel Mac's runner is 2.5 times slower than Linux); its overrides replace single budgets.
A leg that is more than twice as slow as the others is investigated, never loosened.
Ratio budgets (the decoder and waveform-analysis responsiveness limits, 1.5 times idle) are in those benches and are the same on every leg: a ratio compares a leg with itself, so no scale applies.

recorded_only.match_storage: bench_match_storage.py measures what storing match attempts costs (rows and megabytes per candidate); it is a size estimate, not a speed, so it is recorded in the run's JSON and has no budget
recorded_only.decoder: bench_decoder.py holds its own ratio budget (RESPONSIVENESS_BUDGET); nothing is scaled
recorded_only.waveform_analysis: bench_waveform_analysis.py holds its own ratio budget (RESPONSIVENESS_BUDGET); nothing is scaled

library._basis: Windows 11 desktop, performance.md, times 1.5; facet_small_ms: estimate (the guide's 7 and 12 ms predate the facet queries; 33 and 57 ms on Linux, times 1.5); statistics_* are the Phase 15/16 budgets

migrations._basis: m0025: the Phase 16 budget (1 s; 324 ms recorded). m0027: estimate, 58 ms on Linux, floored at 1 s

search_keys._basis: m0033: about 0.6 s recorded at HARDEN-06 and 1.07 s on Linux, times 1.5; the rest: estimates from a Linux run (m0032 0.28 s, search 1.3 ms, count 30 ms)

engine_start._basis: estimates from a Linux run on 308 MB (first /health 0.69 s from source, launch copy 2.1 s, library ok 2.1 s, one migration pending 3.6 s, quick_check 0.74 s), about 4 times that; the packaged one-file engine on a Mac takes about 10 s to unpack on a cold start, so the Macs have their own first_health_ms

tag_write._basis: estimate: 1,000 files through the checked copy took 2.95 s on Linux; Windows is slower (fsync, antivirus)

e2e._basis: estimates (nothing was measured in the packaged app but the renderer: 186-222 MB, times 1.5): the import is the engine's 10.9 s times 1.5 plus the job's own overhead
